script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 26. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Right now, invisible waves are traveling through the air, entering your ear, bouncing off the tiniest bones in your body, and becoming electrical signals your brain interprets as sound.  Hearing is vibration transformed—air movement becoming meaning.

The three smallest bones in your body—hammer, anvil, and stirrup—are in your middle ear. Together, they amplify sound vibrations 20x before passing them to the inner ear. These bones fit on a penny and enable all hearing. In your cochlea, 16,000 hair cells detect vibrations and convert them to electrical signals.  Different areas respond to different frequencies.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: We perceive only a narrow slice of reality.  Hearing reminds us that there's always more happening than we can detect.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Sound Attention - Listen Deeper.

Here's your activity: Close your eyes for 60 seconds and count how many distinct sounds you can hear—near, far, constant, intermittent. We usually filter out most sounds. How many were you missing before you paid attention? This helps you develop deeper listening awareness.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how your ears work can be applied to sound attention - listen deeper. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
